daten.vorhaben.wunder_ephesos.name: Ephesus: master plan for excavation and visitor management
daten.vorhaben.wunder_ephesos.text: A project spanning decades for the port city of antiquity: excavations, reconstruction of selected buildings, routes for visitors and a museum at the foot of the hill. The model is the national programme “Geleceğe Miras” (Heritage for the Future), which began in Ephesus in 2023.
daten.vorhaben.wunder_ephesos.kehrseite: A mass destination: visitor pressure wears down the site, and residents of Selçuk complain about noise and prices.
daten.vorhaben.wunder_antakya.name: Antakya: rebuilding the old town
daten.vorhaben.wunder_antakya.text: The city where the disciples were first called Christians lost most of its historic fabric in the 2023 earthquake. Reconstruction brings back alleys, churches, the synagogue and mosques and fully reopens the mosaic museum.
daten.vorhaben.wunder_antakya.kehrseite: Those who return need housing first: the cultural project competes with housing construction for building capacity and administrative power.
daten.vorhaben.wunder_goebekli.name: Göbekli Tepe: visitor centre and research campus
daten.vorhaben.wunder_goebekli.text: Humanity's oldest known monumental site gets a visitor centre with visitor management, a research building with workshops and a link to the sister sites of the Taş Tepeler project.
daten.vorhaben.wunder_goebekli.kehrseite: 750,000 visitors in 2024 are already a lot; without visitor management the site suffers.
daten.vorhaben.wunder_ani.name: Opening Ani: border crossing, museum, restoration
daten.vorhaben.wunder_ani.text: The medieval capital lies right on the border with Armenia. An open crossing, a museum and the stabilisation of the buildings make it a place of understanding and a touchstone of normalisation.
daten.vorhaben.wunder_ani.kehrseite: Nationalists see it as a concession to Armenia, and Azerbaijan watches every sign of rapprochement.
daten.vorhaben.wunder_kappadokien.name: Cappadocia: protection plan for the rock landscape
daten.vorhaben.wunder_kappadokien.text: Limiting balloon launches, managing visitors and securing the rock churches: Turkey's most famous landscape is to stay what it is.
daten.vorhaben.wunder_kappadokien.kehrse: Balloon operators and hotels lose revenue if the number of launches is capped.
daten.vorhaben.programm_erbe_zukunft.nam: Heritage for the Future: national programme for excavation and restoration
daten.vorhaben.programm_erbe_zukunft.tex: A programme for hundreds of excavation sites and monuments across the country, with staff, workshops and museums, modelled on the “Geleceğe Miras” programme (since 2023: 251 excavation sites, over 5,000 employees).
daten.vorhaben.programm_erbe_zukunft.keh: Ties up restorers and building capacity for years; other building projects have to wait their turn.
daten.vorhaben.serie_kirchen7.name: Route of the Seven Churches
daten.vorhaben.serie_kirchen7.text: A pilgrimage and cultural route to the seven churches of Revelation: Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamon, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia and Laodicea. All seven lie in western Turkey.
daten.vorhaben.serie_kirchen7.kehrseite: Pilgrim flows strain the sites, and some conservatives view the Christian focus critically.
daten.vorhaben.serie_seldschuken.name: Seljuk Route
daten.vorhaben.serie_seldschuken.text: From Konya via Beyşehir and Divriği to Ahlat: mosques, hospitals and tombs of the Seljuk era.
daten.vorhaben.serie_seldschuken.kehrsei: The route lies away from the coasts; without transport links few visitors come.
daten.vorhaben.serie_sinan.name: Sinan Route
daten.vorhaben.serie_sinan.text: Süleymaniye in Istanbul and Selimiye in Edirne: two masterpieces of the architect Sinan.
daten.vorhaben.serie_sinan.kehrseite: Edirne lies on the border with Greece and Bulgaria; travellers need fast crossings.
daten.vorhaben.serie_tas_tepeler.name: Taş Tepeler Route
daten.vorhaben.serie_tas_tepeler.text: Göbekli Tepe, Karahan Tepe and Balıklıgöl: the Stone Age as it becomes visible in south-eastern Anatolia.
daten.vorhaben.serie_tas_tepeler.kehrsei: 750,000 visitors (2024) are already a lot for Göbekli Tepe; without visitor management the site suffers.
daten.vorhaben.serie_byzanz.name: Byzantine Route
daten.vorhaben.serie_byzanz.text: Hagia Sophia, Cappadocia, Myra, Sumela, İznik and the Phanar: traces of the Christian East.
daten.vorhaben.serie_byzanz.kehrseite: The use of Hagia Sophia remains contentious; any change to the visiting rules is read politically.
daten.vorhaben.serie_vielvoelker.name: Route of the Communities
daten.vorhaben.serie_vielvoelker.text: Synagogues, monasteries, churches and old towns where Jews, Armenians, Syriacs and Greeks lived and live: Sardis, Istanbul, Akdamar, Mor Gabriel, Antakya, Mardin, Ani, Edirne.
daten.vorhaben.serie_vielvoelker.kehrsei: Part of the majority views the emphasis on minorities with suspicion; questions of use at the sites are renegotiated.
daten.vorhaben.infra_marmaray.name: Marmaray
daten.vorhaben.infra_marmaray.text: Rail tunnel under the Bosphorus: opened on 29.10.2013, full line 12.03.2019, 75,000 passengers per hour and direction. Built from 2004 with a Japanese loan (111 bn yen); finds at Yenikapı delayed it by about four years.
daten.vorhaben.infra_marmaray.kehrseite: A tunnel in earthquake country: maintenance and seismic safety tie up administrative power.
daten.vorhaben.infra_osmangazi.name: Osmangazi Bridge
daten.vorhaben.infra_osmangazi.text: Suspension bridge across the Gulf of İzmit, opened on 01.07.2016, built and operated privately (BOT). The state guarantees 40,000 vehicles a day; below that it pays the difference. The Istanbul–İzmir route becomes about 140 km shorter.
daten.vorhaben.infra_osmangazi.kehrseite: The guarantee binds the budget: if traffic stays below the target, the state pays the difference.
daten.vorhaben.infra_flughafen.name: Istanbul Airport
daten.vorhaben.infra_flughafen.text: Opened on 29.10.2018 after construction from May 2015, operated as a BOT for 25 years; 90 million passengers a year in the first stage. 657,950 trees were removed for its construction, and officially 27 workers died.
daten.vorhaben.infra_flughafen.kehrseite: A hub is a target: operation and security tie up administrative power, and the construction is not forgotten (forest, dead workers).
daten.vorhaben.infra_yht.name: High-speed rail
daten.vorhaben.infra_yht.text: Ankara–Eskişehir 2009, –Konya 2011, –Istanbul 2014, –Sivas 2023: 1,385 km, 12.4 million passengers in 2024. Extension to İzmir is planned.
daten.vorhaben.infra_yht.kehrseite: Tracks, signals and trains age; without maintenance delays and cancellations become noticeable.
daten.vorhaben.infra_canakkale1915.name: 1915 Çanakkale Bridge
daten.vorhaben.infra_canakkale1915.text: Suspension bridge across the Dardanelles, construction from March 2017, opened on 18.03.2022, 2,023 m span. The state guaranteed 16.4 million crossings a year; actual use was well below that.
daten.vorhaben.infra_canakkale1915.kehrs: A guarantee above demand: the budget carries the gap as long as use does not rise.
daten.vorhaben.infra_gap.name: Southeastern Anatolia Project (GAP) with the Atatürk Dam
daten.vorhaben.infra_gap.text: 22 dams and 19 power plants on the Euphrates and Tigris; the Atatürk Dam (built 1983 to 1990) supplies 2,400 MW and irrigates 4,760 km². Ilısu (2020) flooded Hasankeyf.
daten.vorhaben.infra_gap.kehrseite: Water downstream: Iraq and Syria demand flow volumes; every dry season sharpens the dispute.
daten.vorhaben.infra_btk.name: Baku–Tbilisi–Kars railway
daten.vorhaben.infra_btk.text: 826 km, opened on 30.10.2017; in full operation since 02.06.2026, passenger service Kars–Tbilisi still missing. Links Turkey via Georgia and Azerbaijan with the Caspian Sea.
daten.vorhaben.infra_btk.kehrseite: The line depends on two neighbours: Georgian domestic politics and Azerbaijani interests set the pace too.
daten.vorhaben.infra_stromnetz.name: Transmission grid (TEİAŞ)
daten.vorhaben.infra_stromnetz.text: 72,000 km of lines and eleven connections abroad. The nationwide blackout of 2015 exposed the weak east-west axis.
daten.vorhaben.infra_stromnetz.kehrseite: An old grid with many bottlenecks: renewables and new power plants only get through if the lines grow with them.
daten.vorhaben.infra_akkuyu.name: Akkuyu nuclear power plant
daten.vorhaben.infra_akkuyu.text: Four units of 1,114 MW each, about ten per cent of electricity demand; Rosatom builds, owns and operates it (2010 agreement). In September 2026 cold tests are running, fuel has not yet been loaded. Sanctions complicate payments.
daten.vorhaben.infra_akkuyu.kehrseite: Russia builds, owns and operates it: a dependency for decades, plus safety worries in earthquake country.
daten.vorhaben.infra_wiederaufbau.name: Reconstruction in the earthquake zone
daten.vorhaben.infra_wiederaufbau.text: After the earthquake of 06.02.2023 the government promised 319,000 homes within a year; by February 2025, 201,431 had been handed over, and the target was raised to 453,000 by the end of 2025. Around 200,000 workers on some 3,500 sites.
daten.vorhaben.infra_wiederaufbau.kehrse: Promise against delivery: every delay is read as a broken promise, and building demand drives up prices.
daten.vorhaben.infra_kanal_istanbul.name: Kanal Istanbul
daten.vorhaben.infra_kanal_istanbul.text: An artificial waterway of about 45 km between the Black Sea and the Sea of Marmara, announced on 27.04.2011. Work on the Sazlıdere bridge began on 26.06.2021; according to reports from May 2025, excavation has not begun.
daten.vorhaben.infra_kanal_istanbul.kehr: Drinking water from the Terkos and Durusu area and the Montreux Convention (straits regime): environmental groups, the opposition and residents reject it.
daten.vorhaben.infra_yht_izmir.name: Ankara–İzmir high-speed rail
daten.vorhaben.infra_yht_izmir.text: Linking the capital with the Aegean via Afyon, Uşak and Manisa. An opening date (provisionally 2027) is unconfirmed.
daten.vorhaben.infra_yht_izmir.kehrseite: Ties up building capacity for years; farmers along the route lose land.
daten.vorhaben.infra_strom_ost.name: East-west power axis
daten.vorhaben.infra_strom_ost.text: Lines and substations that bring power from the west and south to the east and prevent outages.
daten.vorhaben.infra_strom_ost.kehrseite: Routes cross pastures and protected areas; residents sue against pylons.
daten.vorhaben.infra_btk_personen.name: Kars–Tbilisi railway: passenger service
daten.vorhaben.infra_btk_personen.text: The missing passenger connection on the Baku–Tbilisi–Kars railway: passengers instead of just freight.
daten.vorhaben.infra_btk_personen.kehrse: A second track for passengers ties up building capacity and needs coordination with Georgia.
daten.vorhaben.infra_bosporus_tunnel3.te: A third crossing tunnel under the Bosphorus for road and rail, announced for years.
daten.vorhaben.infra_bosporus_tunnel3.ke: Another tunnel in earthquake country: construction and operation are expensive and risky.
daten.vorhaben.infra_wasser_ost.name: Water pipelines and storage in the east
daten.vorhaben.infra_wasser_ost.text: Pipelines, storage and irrigation for the provinces hit hardest by dry spells.
daten.vorhaben.infra_wasser_ost.kehrseit: Water for the east is missing downstream: the dispute with Iraq grows if more is drawn off.
daten.vorhaben.infra_glasfaser.name: Fibre to the village
daten.vorhaben.infra_glasfaser.text: Fibre and mobile coverage even where nobody has invested so far.
daten.vorhaben.infra_glasfaser.kehrseite: For small places the roll-out never pays off: it remains permanently dependent on subsidies.
daten.vorhaben.infra_sozialwohnungen.nam: Social housing programme of the housing agency (TOKİ)
daten.vorhaben.infra_sozialwohnungen.tex: A programme for affordable housing in cities with high rents. The housing agency TOKİ has been building since 1984.
daten.vorhaben.infra_sozialwohnungen.keh: New building on the edge of town: journeys get longer, and builders push up prices when building capacity is scarce.
daten.vorhaben.infra_sinop.name: Sinop nuclear power plant
daten.vorhaben.infra_sinop.text: A second nuclear power plant on the Black Sea; the partner is undecided.
daten.vorhaben.infra_sinop.kehrseite: Earthquake country and a site by the sea: local resistance, and the choice of partner decides a new dependency.
daten.vorhaben.recht_aym.name: Constitutional Court
daten.vorhaben.recht_aym.text: 15 members: the president appoints 12 (3 from the Court of Cassation, 2 from the Council of State, 3 on the proposal of the Council of Higher Education, 4 freely), parliament elects 3. Individual applications have existed since 23.09.2012; in 2024 a case took 512 days on average (+61 per cent).
daten.vorhaben.recht_aym.kehrseite: Whoever fills the seats shapes the court: every appointment is a choice between loyalty and independence.
daten.vorhaben.recht_hsk.name: Council of Judges and Prosecutors (HSK)
daten.vorhaben.recht_hsk.text: 13 members, chaired by the justice minister; the president appoints 4, parliament elects 7 (2/3, then 3/5, then lot). The council decides on appointment, transfer and promotion; investigations against judges require the minister's permission. No member is elected by fellow judges.
daten.vorhaben.recht_hsk.kehrseite: The council holds the judiciary in its hand: whoever controls it controls careers, and whoever frees it loses control.
daten.vorhaben.recht_vollzug.name: Prison system
daten.vorhaben.recht_vollzug.text: 304,956 places for 433,520 prisoners in August 2026, about 142 per cent; 65,227 are in pre-trial detention.
daten.vorhaben.recht_vollzug.kehrseite: Overcrowded prisons harm the reputation of the judiciary and rehabilitation; new places alone do not solve it.
daten.vorhaben.recht_anwaltskammern.name: Bar associations
daten.vorhaben.recht_anwaltskammern.text: 80 bar associations. A 2020 law allows additional bars from 5,000 lawyers (Istanbul, Ankara, İzmir); all 80 bars rejected it, and the Constitutional Court dismissed the challenge.
daten.vorhaben.recht_anwaltskammern.kehr: Free lawyers are inconvenient: whoever splits them gains influence and loses legitimacy.
daten.vorhaben.recht_digitale_justiz.tex: Electronic files, remote hearings and automatic scheduling in all courts.
daten.vorhaben.recht_digitale_justiz.keh: Training and data protection take time; small law firms and older judges struggle to keep up.
daten.vorhaben.recht_justizakademie.name: Judicial academy
daten.vorhaben.recht_justizakademie.text: A training institution for judges, prosecutors and court staff with fixed standards.
daten.vorhaben.recht_justizakademie.kehr: Training takes years; trainers are missing from the courts, and the results only show after the next election.
daten.vorhaben.recht_gefaengnisbau.name: New prisons
daten.vorhaben.recht_gefaengnisbau.text: Additional places in the prison system to reduce overcrowding.
daten.vorhaben.recht_gefaengnisbau.kehrs: More places do not solve the causes: without alternatives to custody they fill up again; staff are lacking.
daten.vorhaben.recht_kavala.name: Implement the rulings in the Kavala case
daten.vorhaben.recht_kavala.text: Proceedings under Article 46(4) of the Convention on Human Rights have been running since February 2022. Implementing the Strasbourg judgment ends them and shows whether the government places rulings above political interests.
daten.vorhaben.recht_kavala.kehrseite: Parts of the camp read it as giving in to Strasbourg; the Court of Cassation and pro-government circles protest.
daten.vorhaben.recht_kammergesetz.name: Law on multiple bar associations
daten.vorhaben.recht_kammergesetz.text: Additional bars in big cities, as the 2020 law provides: the bars can be split, the government gains influence.
daten.vorhaben.recht_kammergesetz.kehrse: All 80 bars rejected the 2020 law; lawyers march. Pushing it through wins support in the camp but costs legitimacy.
daten.vorhaben.recht_zielfristen.name: Target deadlines and performance pressure for judges
daten.vorhaben.recht_zielfristen.text: Every judge is measured by caseload completion figures; the council evaluates performance.
daten.vorhaben.recht_zielfristen.kehrsei: Judges rule faster and more superficially, appeals increase, and those who do not deliver fear for their careers.
daten.vorhaben.mil_drohnen.name: Drone fleet (Bayraktar TB2, Akıncı, TB3)
daten.vorhaben.mil_drohnen.text: Agreements on the TB2 with 34 countries, on the Akıncı with 10; the takeover of Piaggio (30.06.2025) and TB3 operations from the carrier Anadolu (October 2025) extend the fleet.
daten.vorhaben.mil_drohnen.kehrseite: Export licences are political: whoever supplies gains customers and enemies; conflicts with buyer countries damage the country's standing.
daten.vorhaben.mil_anadolu.name: Helicopter carrier TCG Anadolu and frigates
daten.vorhaben.mil_anadolu.text: The Anadolu (2023) carries drones and helicopters; in addition come the frigates of the İstif class (the sixth was launched in July 2026).
daten.vorhaben.mil_anadolu.kehrseite: Large ships tie up shipyards, crews and administrative power, and their deployment is politically visible.
daten.vorhaben.mil_s400.name: S-400 air defence (in storage)
daten.vorhaben.mil_s400.text: Two batteries and over 120 missiles (July to September 2019); cannot be integrated into NATO air defence. The US sanction (CAATSA) against the defence agency SSB has applied since December 2020.
daten.vorhaben.mil_s400.kehrseite: As long as the S-400s are in the country, Washington blocks the F-35 (NDAA §1245).
daten.vorhaben.mil_f16.name: F-16 Block 70
daten.vorhaben.mil_f16.text: 40 ordered; 79 modernisation kits were cancelled in November 2024 in favour of domestic modernisation. The fleet stands at 235 F-16s.
daten.vorhaben.mil_f16.kehrseite: Dependence on American approval for spare parts and munitions.
daten.vorhaben.mil_stahlkuppel.name: Steel Dome: layered air defence
daten.vorhaben.mil_stahlkuppel.text: 47 systems worth 460 million USD entered the inventory on 27.08.2025; Siper Block I has been operational since January 2026, and the 6.5 bn USD contract was signed on 26.11.2025. Components from Aselsan follow from 2028 to 2032.
daten.vorhaben.mil_stahlkuppel.kehrseite: A system of many sensors and effectors: integration with NATO systems is open.
daten.vorhaben.mil_altay.name: Altay T1 main battle tank
daten.vorhaben.mil_altay.text: Series production began on 05.09.2025, in service since 28.10.2025. The first 40 or more get a Korean powerpack; the engine from BMC Power is to follow from the end of 2026.
daten.vorhaben.mil_altay.kehrseite: The engine comes from Korea: self-sufficiency is not yet achieved.
daten.vorhaben.mil_kaan.name: KAAN fighter jet Block 10
daten.vorhaben.mil_kaan.text: First flight in February 2024; a contract for 20 was signed on 08.05.2026, Indonesia ordered 48. The engine so far comes from General Electric (F110); a domestic TF35000 is announced for 2032.
daten.vorhaben.mil_kaan.kehrseite: As long as the engine comes from the USA, Washington has a veto over exports and deliveries.
daten.vorhaben.mil_kaan_motor.name: Domestic TF35000 engine
daten.vorhaben.mil_kaan_motor.text: A domestically developed fighter engine ends the dependence on American approvals. 2032 is named as the target.
daten.vorhaben.mil_kaan_motor.kehrseite: Years of development with an uncertain outcome; engineers and test stands are missing elsewhere.
daten.vorhaben.mil_eurofighter.name: Eurofighter Typhoon
daten.vorhaben.mil_eurofighter.text: 20 new jets, up to 8 bn pounds (27.10.2025); a support contract of 25.03.2026 provides for training 10 flight instructors and about 100 technicians in Britain. First deliveries in 2030 according to press reports.
daten.vorhaben.mil_eurofighter.kehrseite: Delivery from 2030 at the earliest: until then the air force has a gap.
daten.vorhaben.mil_f35.name: F-35
daten.vorhaben.mil_f35.text: Excluded since July 2019. The law NDAA §1245 requires that no S-400 remain in the country; on 22.07.2026 the US State Department reported the condition unmet.
daten.vorhaben.mil_f35.kehrseite: The tie to Washington becomes tighter: software, spare parts and use are subject to American approval.
daten.vorhaben.mil_s400_abgeben.name: Hand over or sell the S-400
daten.vorhaben.mil_s400_abgeben.text: The Russian batteries leave the country. That clears the block on the F-35 and ends the CAATSA sanction, but costs face and Moscow's goodwill.
daten.vorhaben.mil_s400_abgeben.kehrseit: A loss of face at home and in Moscow; air defence has a gap until the Steel Dome stands.
daten.vorhaben.mil_tf2000.name: TF-2000 destroyer
daten.vorhaben.mil_tf2000.text: An air-defence destroyer from a domestic shipyard.
daten.vorhaben.mil_tf2000.kehrseite: A large ship with schedule risk: delays are likely, and the shipyard is missing elsewhere.
daten.vorhaben.mil_huerjet.name: Hürjet: trainer and export
daten.vorhaben.mil_huerjet.text: The Hürjet jet trainer trains pilots and is an export product: Spain has signed a contract for 30.
daten.vorhaben.mil_huerjet.kehrseite: An export success requires customer support and spare parts for decades.
daten.vorhaben.doktrin_drohnen.name: Doctrine: drone network
daten.vorhaben.doktrin_drohnen.text: Unmanned systems carry reconnaissance and strike; the forces are built around the network.
daten.vorhaben.doktrin_drohnen.kehrseite: Pilots and tank officers lose status; against an opponent with strong air defences the network would be put to the test.
The armed forces rely on sensors, interceptors and data links that protect the airspace in layers.
Expensive to maintain: sensors, interceptors and data links tie up administrative power.
daten.vorhaben.doktrin_autonomie.name: Doctrine: strategic autonomy
daten.vorhaben.doktrin_autonomie.text: No system without a domestic alternative: development and production at home take precedence over purchases.
daten.vorhaben.doktrin_autonomie.kehrsei: Less tied to allies: less leverage for Washington and Brussels, but also less backing.
daten.vorhaben.sr_energiedeckel.name: Energy price cap (BOTAŞ)
daten.vorhaben.sr_energiedeckel.text: The state gas importer sells gas and power below the import price: it relieves households immediately.
daten.vorhaben.sr_energiedeckel.kehrseit: The state bears the difference between import price and cap: the budget and the foreign-exchange balance pay, and saving is not rewarded.
daten.vorhaben.sr_kreditgarantien.name: Credit guarantee fund
daten.vorhaben.sr_kreditgarantien.text: The state guarantees loans to firms that would otherwise get none.
daten.vorhaben.sr_kreditgarantien.kehrse: A contingent liability: in a wave of defaults the guarantee becomes real, and the markets factor it in beforehand.
daten.vorhaben.sr_wechselkursschutz.name: Deposits with exchange-rate guarantee
daten.vorhaben.sr_wechselkursschutz.text: Savers who invest in lira are compensated by the state for the loss of value against the dollar.
daten.vorhaben.sr_wechselkursschutz.kehr: The state bears the exchange-rate risk: every depreciation becomes a bill, and exiting is expensive.
daten.vorhaben.sr_staatsbanken.name: Credit steering through state banks
daten.vorhaben.sr_staatsbanken.text: The state banks lend according to political guidelines: to construction, agriculture and exporters.
daten.vorhaben.sr_staatsbanken.kehrseite: Loans follow politics, not risk: defaults at the state banks end up in the budget.
daten.vorhaben.sr_vermoegensfonds.name: Sovereign wealth fund
daten.vorhaben.sr_vermoegensfonds.text: A fund holds state stakes outside the normal budget and can invest quickly.
daten.vorhaben.sr_vermoegensfonds.kehrse: A fund outside the budget has little oversight: accusations of cronyism follow.
daten.vorhaben.welt_korridor_abkommen.na: Transit agreement for the Middle Corridor
daten.vorhaben.welt_korridor_abkommen.te: A package of treaties with Georgia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and China on transit, tariffs and border clearance. The Middle Corridor runs via Georgia and Azerbaijan, by ferry across the Caspian Sea and through Kazakhstan to China.
daten.vorhaben.welt_korridor_abkommen.ke: Every country demands a price: fees, quotas, commitments. Russia reads the corridor as a bypass, and Moscow and Beijing are rarely satisfied at the same time.
daten.vorhaben.welt_korridor_abkommen.an: The model is the Trans-Caspian route, which has grown strongly in importance since 2022.
daten.vorhaben.welt_korridor_terminals.n: Terminals, ferries and freight rail on the Caspian Sea
daten.vorhaben.welt_korridor_terminals.t: Transhipment points, ferries and additional tracks between Kars, Baku and the eastern shore of the Caspian Sea: the bottleneck of the Middle Corridor widens.
daten.vorhaben.welt_korridor_terminals.k: The ferries across the Caspian Sea are the bottleneck: waiting times, weather and the neighbours set the pace.
daten.vorhaben.welt_korridor_terminals.a: Analogous to the terminal expansions on the Caspian Sea (Baku-Alat, Aktau).
daten.vorhaben.welt_autobahn_china.name: Motorway to China (Middle Corridor)
daten.vorhaben.welt_autobahn_china.text: A continuous motorway from Anatolia via Georgia, Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan to the Chinese border: over six thousand kilometres of road, dozens of border crossings and no country that decides alone.
daten.vorhaben.welt_autobahn_china.kehrs: The road to China is also a road for China: loans, tariffs and dependence. Georgia, Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan demand fees, and Washington and Brussels ask whom the route benefits.
daten.vorhaben.welt_autobahn_china.anker: Analogous to the Western Europe–Western China motorway through Kazakhstan (over 2,700 kilometres there alone, built with loans from several sources).
daten.vorhaben.welt_hsr_china.name: High-speed rail to China (Middle Corridor)
daten.vorhaben.welt_hsr_china.text: A high-speed line from Ankara via Kars, Tbilisi, Baku and Kazakhstan to the Chinese border: the longest new line the country would ever have built, across seas, mountains and five states.
daten.vorhaben.welt_hsr_china.kehrseite: Whoever builds the high-speed line ties themselves to one supplier: technology, loans and spare parts come from one source. The West sees a gateway to China, the neighbours a toll.
daten.vorhaben.welt_hsr_china.anker: Analogous to the China–Laos railway (1,035 kilometres, around six billion US dollars, 2016 to 2021) and the Jakarta–Bandung high-speed line (142 kilometres, around 7.3 billion US dollars after high overruns).
daten.vorhaben.welt_megahafen.name: Mersin mega-port
daten.vorhaben.welt_megahafen.text: A port the size of the Mediterranean's great hubs: container terminals, industrial zones and rail connection on the south coast.
daten.vorhaben.welt_megahafen.kehrseite: A port of this size attracts traffic, dust and speculation; residents, fishermen and environmental groups fight back, and the competition in the Mediterranean never sleeps.
daten.vorhaben.welt_megahafen.anker: Analogous to Tanger Med in Morocco and the port of Jebel Ali in Dubai (multi-billion projects over two decades).
daten.vorhaben.welt_maglev.name: Istanbul–Ankara maglev
daten.vorhaben.welt_maglev.text: A magnetic levitation line linking the two largest cities in under an hour: faster than any train the country has, and a technology that only a few lines in the world carry so far.
daten.vorhaben.welt_maglev.kehrseite: A line hardly anyone needs costs more than any other railway in the country: power, routes and maintenance are without precedent here, and every passenger is subsidised by the taxpayer.
daten.vorhaben.welt_maglev.anker: Analogous to the Chūō Shinkansen in Japan (Tokyo–Nagoya–Osaka maglev, construction began 2014, opening only expected after the 2030s, costs far above the first estimate).
daten.vorhaben.welt_bruecke_zypern.name: Bridge or tunnel to Cyprus
daten.vorhaben.welt_bruecke_zypern.text: A fixed link from the south coast to Northern Cyprus, across more than seventy kilometres of open sea. Technically conceivable, politically blocked: it presupposes a settlement of the Cyprus question.
daten.vorhaben.welt_bruecke_zypern.kehrs: A bridge is also a border crossing: nationalists on both sides read it as surrender, Greece and the EU set conditions, and an attack or a storm paralyses it.
daten.vorhaben.welt_bruecke_zypern.anker: Analogous to the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau bridge (55 kilometres, around 20 billion US dollars, built 2009 to 2018); the route to Cyprus would be longer and politically blocked.
daten.vorhaben.stadt_satellit_ost.name: East Istanbul satellite city
daten.vorhaben.stadt_satellit_ost.text: A new town for half a million people on the eastern edge of the metropolis: housing, schools, public transport and businesses planned all at once.
daten.vorhaben.stadt_satellit_ost.kehrse: New building on forest and watershed land at the city edge: the city keeps sprawling, journeys get longer, and those who wanted to buy cheaply end up paying with time in traffic.
daten.vorhaben.stadt_satellit_ost.anker: Analogous to the satellite cities around Seoul (new towns such as Bundang, built from the late 1980s).
daten.vorhaben.stadt_hauptstadt_neu.name: New capital in Central Anatolia
daten.vorhaben.stadt_hauptstadt_neu.text: Government, parliament and ministries move to a newly built city in the heart of the country. Ankara remains a metropolis but loses the state.
daten.vorhaben.stadt_hauptstadt_neu.kehr: Moving the state means moving power: civil servants, embassies and companies follow reluctantly, parts of Ankara decline, and every change of minister costs years until the administration works again.
daten.vorhaben.stadt_hauptstadt_neu.anke: Analogous to Nusantara in Indonesia (around 30 billion US dollars planned, construction began 2022, government move repeatedly postponed) and Egypt's new administrative capital.
daten.vorhaben.stadt_unterwasser.name: Underwater city in the Sea of Marmara
daten.vorhaben.stadt_unterwasser.text: An inhabited city below the water's surface, with its own air, energy and rescue. So far there are only research stations for a few people and a few weeks.
daten.vorhaben.stadt_unterwasser.kehrsei: Pressure, power, air and rescue: every failure is a disaster with no way out, insurers decline, and in an earthquake zone by the sea every assumption is too optimistic.
daten.vorhaben.stadt_unterwasser.anker: Without a real model; the largest inhabited underwater facilities so far are research stations such as the Aquarius habitat off Florida.
daten.vorhaben.energie_hvdc_europa.name: Power link to Europe (direct-current cable)
daten.vorhaben.energie_hvdc_europa.text: A high-voltage direct-current link via Greece or Bulgaria into the European grid: power in both directions, as long as both sides want it.
daten.vorhaben.energie_hvdc_europa.kehrs: Whoever exports power also imports prices: when Europe is short, prices rise at home, and Brussels sets conditions on market rules.
daten.vorhaben.energie_hvdc_europa.anker: Analogous to NordLink between Germany and Norway (623 kilometres, in operation since 2021, around two billion euros).
daten.vorhaben.energie_smr.name: Fleet of small modular reactors
daten.vorhaben.energie_smr.text: A series of small reactors built in factories and set up at several sites: less construction site, more technology, faster and cheaper – so the hope goes.
daten.vorhaben.energie_smr.kehrseite: New technology, expensive first plants: the licensing risk lies with the state, waste disposal is unresolved, and sites provoke resistance in every province.
daten.vorhaben.energie_smr.anker: Analogous to the cancelled NuScale project in Utah (costs rose from around 5.3 to 9.3 billion US dollars before it was cancelled in 2023).
daten.vorhaben.energie_brennstoffkreisla: Own facilities for fuel and reprocessing, so that the reactors do not depend on foreign suppliers. The facilities are under the control of the atomic energy agency.
Enrichment is dual-use: the atomic energy agency inspects, the neighbours and the West ask about the purpose, and threats of sanctions are closer than with any power plant.
Analogous to the enrichment programmes of smaller nuclear states that were under inspection and threat of sanctions for years.
A national research programme on nuclear fusion with institutes, participation in international facilities and doctoral students from all over the world. It will not supply electricity in the foreseeable future.
Money for research with no return this term: opponents ask about schools and roads, and the best people go where the facilities are.
Analogous to ITER (costs rose from a planned five to over twenty billion euros, research operation from 2034 at the earliest).
daten.vorhaben.energie_fusion_testreakto: A large experimental facility that creates and holds fusion plasma: the step from research to technology. Worldwide, a consortium of states has been building a single facility of this kind for decades.
Every delay costs billions, and success is uncertain: if the plasma fails, one of the most expensive experimental facilities in the world remains.
Analogous to ITER in France (construction began 2007, first plasma repeatedly postponed, costs several times above plan).
Fusion power plant on the grid
A power plant that feeds electricity from nuclear fusion into the grid: almost inexhaustible energy without long-lived waste. No country has yet operated a fusion power plant.
The most expensive bet in the country's history: decades of money without power, a technology that does not yet exist, and a change of government can cancel it at any time.
Without a real model; estimates for the first fusion power plants range from decades to sums in the high tens of billions.
daten.vorhaben.wasser_konya.name: Water transfer to the Konya basin
daten.vorhaben.wasser_konya.text: Canals and tunnels bring water from the mountains in the south and west to the Konya plain, where the water table has been falling for years and sinkholes tear open the fields.
daten.vorhaben.wasser_konya.kehrseite: The water is missing where it comes from: the source areas and their rivers lose out, farmers and towns fight over every cubic metre.
daten.vorhaben.wasser_konya.anker: Analogous to the central route of China's South–North Water Transfer (opened 2014, costs in the tens of billions).
daten.vorhaben.wasser_entsalzung.name: Seawater desalination on the south coast
daten.vorhaben.wasser_entsalzung.text: Large desalination plants on the Mediterranean for the coastal cities and the hinterland: water that does not depend on rain, but on electricity.
daten.vorhaben.wasser_entsalzung.kehrsei: Desalination eats electricity and leaves brine in the sea: the water bill becomes an electricity bill, and fishermen complain about the water off the plants.
daten.vorhaben.wasser_entsalzung.anker: Analogous to the large desalination plants in the Gulf, which supply much of the neighbouring states' drinking water.
daten.vorhaben.wasser_friedensleitung.na: Peace pipeline: water for the Middle East
daten.vorhaben.wasser_friedensleitung.te: A long-distance pipeline from the water-rich rivers of the south to Syria, Jordan and the Gulf states: water in exchange for relations. The plan was put forward once before in the 1980s and never built.
daten.vorhaben.wasser_friedensleitung.ke: Water as leverage: whoever controls the pipeline controls the tap. Iraq, already at odds over the Euphrates and Tigris, feels threatened, and Israel as a buyer is political dynamite at home.
daten.vorhaben.wasser_friedensleitung.an: The model is the Peace Pipeline plan of the 1980s (pipelines from the Seyhan and Ceyhan southwards), which was never built.
daten.vorhaben.raum_agentur.name: Expand the space agency
daten.vorhaben.raum_agentur.text: The space agency (TUA, founded 2018) gets staff, laboratories and its own budget; a space law sets out responsibilities between the agency, industry and the military.
daten.vorhaben.raum_agentur.kehrseite: An agency without rockets costs salaries and patience: results only show in later terms, and critics ask what schools and hospitals get out of it.
daten.vorhaben.raum_agentur.anker: Analogous to smaller space agencies in their build-up phase, such as India's ISRO (founded 1969).
daten.vorhaben.raum_satelliten.name: Satellite programme (earth observation, communications, navigation)
daten.vorhaben.raum_satelliten.text: Own satellites for earth observation, communications and regional navigation. With Türksat 6A (launched in 2024, on a rocket from the USA) the country shows what it can do and what it still depends on.
daten.vorhaben.raum_satelliten.kehrseite: Satellites age and fail: replacements have to follow, and whoever puts them into orbit sets the pace and the terms.
daten.vorhaben.raum_satelliten.anker: Depending on size, an earth observation satellite costs from a few million to several hundred million US dollars.
daten.vorhaben.raum_bahnhof.name: Spaceport on the south coast
daten.vorhaben.raum_bahnhof.text: A launch site with pads, test stands and an exclusion zone over the sea: whoever wants to launch rockets needs a place that can take them, and neighbours who accept it.
daten.vorhaben.raum_bahnhof.kehrseite: A launch site needs exclusion zones: fishermen, hoteliers and coastal communities lose land and sea, and every rocket is a risk to the neighbours.
daten.vorhaben.raum_bahnhof.anker: Analogous to the Vostochny cosmodrome in Russia (construction from 2012, first launch 2016, costs of several billion US dollars and corruption trials).
daten.vorhaben.raum_traeger.name: Own orbital launch vehicle
daten.vorhaben.raum_traeger.text: A rocket that puts payloads into orbit itself: engines, stages, propellants, test stands. The country would be independent of foreign launches, but every failed launch goes round the world.
daten.vorhaben.raum_traeger.kehrseite: Rocket technology is dual-use: the West and the neighbours ask about the purpose, and every failed launch belongs to the opposition.
daten.vorhaben.raum_traeger.anker: Analogous to Ariane 6 (development around four billion euros, first flight in 2024 instead of 2020).
daten.vorhaben.raum_mondsonde.name: Moon mission (uncrewed, soft landing)
daten.vorhaben.raum_mondsonde.text: A probe flies to the Moon and makes a soft landing. The country would join the few states that have managed it; a failure is just as visible worldwide.
daten.vorhaben.raum_mondsonde.kehrseite: A failure is visible worldwide, and the money for the Moon is missing in everyday life: opponents ask whether the country can afford it.
daten.vorhaben.raum_mondsonde.anker: Analogous to Chandrayaan-3 (India, soft landing in 2023, around 75 million US dollars, after one failed attempt and years of preparation).
daten.vorhaben.raum_orbit_bemannt.name: Crewed mission to orbit
daten.vorhaben.raum_orbit_bemannt.text: A capsule with a crew launched into orbit from home soil. With Alper Gezeravcı's flight to the space station (Axiom-3, January 2024) Turkey has an astronaut; its own mission would be the next step.
daten.vorhaben.raum_orbit_bemannt.kehrse: Human lives at stake: an accident ends the programme and a chapter of the term, and safety standards take years.
daten.vorhaben.raum_orbit_bemannt.anker: Analogous to Gaganyaan (India, approved in 2018 with around 100 billion rupees, first flight postponed several times).
daten.vorhaben.raum_mondbasis.name: Moon base
daten.vorhaben.raum_mondbasis.text: A permanently crewed station on the Moon with its own energy, water and air. No country has yet built such a station.
daten.vorhaben.raum_mondbasis.kehrseite: Decades of money with nothing in return in everyday life: whoever pays saves elsewhere, and a change of government can topple the programme in any year.
daten.vorhaben.raum_mondbasis.anker: Analogous to the US Artemis programme (according to NASA auditors over 90 billion US dollars by 2025 for the return to the Moon, dates postponed several times).
daten.vorhaben.raum_mars.name: Mars mission (crewed)
daten.vorhaben.raum_mars.text: People travel to Mars and return: months of flight, a landing site, life out of a can. No country has ever done it; the technology exists only on paper.
daten.vorhaben.raum_mars.kehrseite: The bill comes long before the result: a lifetime of debt, a risk to lives and reputation, and the crew flies into a life with no way back if something goes wrong.
daten.vorhaben.raum_mars.anker: Analogous to estimates for crewed Mars missions (on the order of hundreds of billions of US dollars); NASA's uncrewed sample return alone was put at over ten billion US dollars.
daten.vorhaben.raum_aufzug.name: Space elevator
daten.vorhaben.raum_aufzug.text: A tether from the equator into orbit, up which loads climb without a rocket: the dream of making spaceflight cheap. A material that could bear such a tether is missing.
daten.vorhaben.raum_aufzug.kehrseite: A venture without precedent: the tether snaps or it does not, and a lifetime of debt depends on it. Every meteorite, every storm and every act of sabotage hits a single structure.
daten.vorhaben.raum_aufzug.anker: Without a real model; so far there is no material that could bear such a tether.
daten.vorhaben.ki_strategie.name: National AI strategy and legal framework
daten.vorhaben.ki_strategie.text: A strategy with goals, responsibilities and rules for the use of artificial intelligence in business, the state and research; plus a law on data, liability and oversight.
daten.vorhaben.ki_strategie.kehrseite: Rules too early slow things down, rules too late do harm: whoever runs oversight has power over the industry, and civil rights campaigners ask who oversees the overseers.
daten.vorhaben.ki_strategie.anker: Analogous to the national AI strategies of small and medium-sized states since 2017; Turkey itself has had a strategy since 2021.
daten.vorhaben.ki_rechenzentren.name: National network of AI data centres
daten.vorhaben.ki_rechenzentren.text: Large data centres with high-performance computers at sites with plenty of power and cooling water: the foundation of any domestic AI.
daten.vorhaben.ki_rechenzentren.kehrseit: Data centres eat power and water: a one-gigawatt campus needs as much electricity as around seven hundred thousand households, and residents end up paying the bill.
daten.vorhaben.ki_rechenzentren.anker: Analogous to the data centre parks of the big cloud providers (several hundred megawatts to over a gigawatt per site).
daten.vorhaben.ki_chipfab.name: Chip factory (semiconductor manufacturing)
daten.vorhaben.ki_chipfab.text: A factory for modern semiconductors: clean rooms, machines from a handful of factories in the world and skilled workers the country hardly has.
daten.vorhaben.ki_chipfab.kehrseite: The factory depends on a few suppliers of machines and chips: US export controls and a dispute with Washington paralyse it, and its water use hits residents and farmers.
daten.vorhaben.ki_chipfab.anker: Analogous to TSMC's chip factories in Arizona (announced in 2020 at twelve billion US dollars, later expanded to over sixty billion, dates postponed) and Intel's cancelled plant in Magdeburg (around thirty billion euros planned, abandoned in 2025).
daten.vorhaben.ki_sprachmodell.name: Own Turkish language model
daten.vorhaben.ki_sprachmodell.text: A large language model trained on Turkish texts and running for public administration, schools and companies, without foreign platforms.
daten.vorhaben.ki_sprachmodell.kehrseite: A state model speaks as the state wishes: the charge of censorship is close at hand, the chips come from suppliers under US export control, and training costs power and time.
daten.vorhaben.ki_sprachmodell.anker: Analogous to the language models of the United Arab Emirates (Falcon) and France (Mistral); according to developers, training a top model costs over a hundred million US dollars.
daten.vorhaben.ki_verwaltung.name: AI in public administration
daten.vorhaben.ki_verwaltung.text: Applications, tax audits and enquiries largely run through AI systems: faster, more uniform and with less room for arbitrariness, and for individual cases.
daten.vorhaben.ki_verwaltung.kehrseite: Surveillance and wrong decisions: whoever the system misclassifies finds no human to correct it; public servants fear for their jobs.
daten.vorhaben.ki_verwaltung.anker: Analogous to the digital administrations of Estonia and South Korea, which offer many services without a trip to the office.
daten.vorhaben.ki_justiz.name: AI-assisted justice
daten.vorhaben.ki_justiz.text: Files are sorted by AI systems, pleadings summarised and draft decisions proposed; judges still decide themselves.
daten.vorhaben.ki_justiz.kehrseite: A proposal that is followed is in effect a decision: errors in the system become wrongful judgments, the reasoning stays unclear, and whoever controls the system controls the direction of rulings.
daten.vorhaben.ki_justiz.anker: Analogous to China's smart courts and pilot projects on AI assistance in European justice systems.
daten.vorhaben.ki_militaer.name: AI battle management and drone swarms
daten.vorhaben.ki_militaer.text: Cooperating drones that recognise targets, coordinate and speed up reconnaissance and defence; the decision on using weapons stays with humans.
daten.vorhaben.ki_militaer.kehrseite: Sanctions risk over chips, disputes on arms control and the question of responsibility: who is liable if a swarm decides wrongly?
daten.vorhaben.ki_militaer.anker: Analogous to the AI programmes of major states' armed forces, tested for years and disputed in arms control.
daten.vorhaben.ki_agi.name: Artificial general intelligence (national major programme)
daten.vorhaben.ki_agi.text: A programme aiming at an AI that masters a broad range of human tasks. Nobody knows whether it can be done; whoever gets there first sets the rules.
daten.vorhaben.ki_agi.kehrseite: A whole country's electricity bill, dependence on a few chip suppliers and a risk no one can contain: failures are expensive, and successes change work and power in ways no government steers.
daten.vorhaben.ki_agi.anker: Analogous to the private Stargate project in the USA (announced in January 2025 with up to 500 billion US dollars over four years).
daten.vorhaben.meer_institut.name: Marine research institute and research vessels
daten.vorhaben.meer_institut.text: An institute with its own fleet for oceanography, fisheries, marine biology and the seabed: the country knows its three seas, the Black Sea, the Sea of Marmara and the Mediterranean, better than its neighbours.
daten.vorhaben.meer_institut.kehrseite: Research at sea is expensive and weather-dependent: the yield is data, not revenue, and fishermen and coastal towns ask what they get out of it.
daten.vorhaben.meer_institut.anker: Analogous to national marine research institutes with their own fleets; research vessels cost tens to hundreds of millions of euros depending on size.
daten.vorhaben.meer_institut.konkurrenz: Marine data are strategic: foreign research vessels cruise the waters, and whoever measures knows where gas and cables lie.
daten.vorhaben.meer_offshore_wind.name: Offshore wind farms (Aegean and Black Sea)
daten.vorhaben.meer_offshore_wind.text: Wind farms at sea, with subsea cables and substation platforms: more wind and more power than on land, but technology the country barely has so far.
daten.vorhaben.meer_offshore_wind.kehrse: Subsea cables, ships and maintenance in salt water are expensive; fishermen, bird migration and coastal tourism push back, and storms knock out installations.
daten.vorhaben.meer_offshore_wind.anker: Analogous to the offshore wind farms in the North Sea, each costing several billion euros.
daten.vorhaben.meer_offshore_wind.konkur: Supply chains for turbines and special vessels are fully booked worldwide; whoever orders first gets served first.
daten.vorhaben.meer_tiefsee_gas.name: Deep-sea gas: expanding the Sakarya field and new wells
daten.vorhaben.meer_tiefsee_gas.text: Further production phases in the Black Sea and drilling in the Mediterranean with the country's own drillships: more domestic gas, a smaller import bill.
daten.vorhaben.meer_tiefsee_gas.kehrseit: The deep sea is costly: drillships, pipelines and insurance; drilling in the Mediterranean runs into maritime boundary disputes with Greece, Cyprus and Egypt.
daten.vorhaben.meer_tiefsee_gas.anker: Analogous to production in the Sakarya field (discovered 2020, production started 2023, expansion over several phases with investments in the billions).
daten.vorhaben.meer_tiefsee_gas.konkurre: Greece, Cyprus and Egypt lodge claims, the EU threatens sanctions, and competitors secure drilling rights and drillships.
daten.vorhaben.meer_hafenautomatisierung: Driverless cranes, automated guided vehicles and a control centre for the big container ports: faster, cheaper and round the clock.
Cranes without drivers, work without dockers: the unions fight back, and a cyber attack paralyses an entire port.
Analogous to the automation of the container terminals in Rotterdam and Shanghai.
The big Mediterranean ports are automating too; cyber attacks on control centres are an everyday occurrence.
daten.vorhaben.meer_uwdrohnen.name: Underwater drones and seabed surveillance
daten.vorhaben.meer_uwdrohnen.text: Uncrewed underwater vehicles for reconnaissance, mine countermeasures and protecting cables and pipelines, plus sensors on the seabed.
daten.vorhaben.meer_uwdrohnen.kehrseite: Sensors and cables on the seabed are vulnerable: sabotage is easy and hard to prove, and whoever listens in there also listens in on the neighbours.
daten.vorhaben.meer_uwdrohnen.anker: Analogous to the underwater drone programmes of larger navies, tested for years.
daten.vorhaben.meer_uwdrohnen.konkurrenz: Russia and Western navies operate their own systems; the seabed is a field of espionage.
daten.vorhaben.meer_uboote.name: National submarine fleet
daten.vorhaben.meer_uboote.text: Submarines of domestic design from domestic shipyards, with their own propulsion, sensors and weapons, to replace the licence builds.
daten.vorhaben.meer_uboote.kehrseite: Submarines tie up shipyards and crews for decades; a design flaw only shows in the water, and the neighbours in the Aegean dispute read every new acquisition as a threat.
daten.vorhaben.meer_uboote.anker: Analogous to Australia's submarine programme under AUKUS (costs to 2050 estimated at up to 368 billion Australian dollars).
daten.vorhaben.meer_uboote.konkurrenz: Suppliers of propulsion and sensors are subject to other states' conditions; competitors tout cheaper offers.
daten.vorhaben.meer_tiefseebergbau.name: Deep-sea mining (manganese nodules and metals)
daten.vorhaben.meer_tiefseebergbau.text: Mining metals on the seabed at depths of several thousand metres: raw materials for batteries from the sea. No country yet mines commercially at this depth.
daten.vorhaben.meer_tiefseebergbau.kehrs: The seabed is a habitat hardly anyone knows: environmental groups, fishermen and many states reject mining, and every accident becomes a global scandal.
daten.vorhaben.meer_tiefseebergbau.anker: So far the International Seabed Authority has not approved any commercial mining.
daten.vorhaben.meer_tiefseebergbau.konku: China, the USA and small island states have secured licence areas; the Seabed Authority demands rules before anyone may mine.
daten.vorhaben.luft_triebwerke.name: Engine development (civil and military)
daten.vorhaben.luft_triebwerke.text: A national engine programme: test stands, materials and manufacturing for engines from drones to fighter jets. Engines are the hardest part of any aircraft.
daten.vorhaben.luft_triebwerke.kehrseite: Engines take decades of experience, licences and suppliers: sanctions hit individual parts, and a single setback costs years.
daten.vorhaben.luft_triebwerke.anker: Analogous to development programmes for fighter engines, which usually take more than a decade.
daten.vorhaben.luft_triebwerke.konkurren: Engine know-how is the industry's best-kept secret: manufacturers and states protect it, and espionage is part of the business.
daten.vorhaben.luft_regionalflugzeug.tex: A passenger aircraft for short and medium routes developed and built at home, certified for the markets where it is to be sold.
daten.vorhaben.luft_regionalflugzeug.keh: Certification takes years, and customers buy on trust: without orders an expensive aircraft stays on the ground, and any crash ends the programme.
daten.vorhaben.luft_regionalflugzeug.ank: Analogous to China's C919 (development from 2008, first flight 2017, certification in 2022 after years of delay).
daten.vorhaben.luft_regionalflugzeug.kon: Boeing, Airbus and the Chinese and Brazilian manufacturers defend their markets with prices, loans and politics.
daten.vorhaben.luft_flugtaxi.name: Air taxi network for big cities
daten.vorhaben.luft_flugtaxi.text: Electric vertical take-off aircraft as urban transport over Istanbul, Ankara and İzmir: air corridors, landing pads, charging infrastructure and oversight for thousands of flights a day.
daten.vorhaben.luft_flugtaxi.kehrseite: Noise, accidents and crowded airspace over cities of millions; flights for the few who can afford them while road traffic below keeps growing.
daten.vorhaben.luft_flugtaxi.anker: Analogous to the air taxi developers, several of which went bankrupt despite billions in investment (such as Volocopter in 2024).
daten.vorhaben.luft_flugtaxi.konkurrenz: Several manufacturers in the USA, Europe and China are vying for the first certifications; some have already failed.
daten.vorhaben.bio_genomik.name: National genome programme (genome centre)
daten.vorhaben.bio_genomik.text: A centre decodes the genomes of hundreds of thousands of volunteers, links them with health data and gives researchers and doctors access: the basis for personalised medicine.
daten.vorhaben.bio_genomik.kehrseite: Genome data are the most sensitive data there are: data protection, discrimination by insurers and employers, and whoever owns the data has power.
daten.vorhaben.bio_genomik.anker: Analogous to UK Biobank (500,000 participants) and national genome programmes in the Middle East.
daten.vorhaben.bio_genomik.konkurrenz: Data brokers and foreign intelligence services are interested in the genomes of an entire population; pharmaceutical companies offer partnerships that demand data.
daten.vorhaben.bio_impfstoffwerk.name: Vaccine and active-ingredient plant
daten.vorhaben.bio_impfstoffwerk.text: A state-supported plant for vaccines and active ingredients, building on experience such as the Turkovac vaccine (approved in 2021): preparedness for the next pandemic and own medicines.
daten.vorhaben.bio_impfstoffwerk.kehrsei: Approval, patents and licences decide success; factories have to run to pay off, and preparedness costs money even without a pandemic.
daten.vorhaben.bio_impfstoffwerk.anker: Analogous to the state-supported vaccine plants built in many countries after 2020; depending on the technology, a vaccine factory costs a few hundred million to over a billion euros.
daten.vorhaben.bio_impfstoffwerk.konkurr: Big pharmaceutical companies cut prices when a state builds its own plants, and defend their patents.
daten.vorhaben.bio_saatgut.name: Seed and agricultural biotechnology
daten.vorhaben.bio_saatgut.text: Breeding drought- and heat-resistant varieties, seed banks and plant genetics laboratories: more harvest with less water.
daten.vorhaben.bio_saatgut.kehrseite: Growing genetically modified crops is banned so far; a change of course divides society. New varieties make farmers dependent on a few seed companies.
daten.vorhaben.bio_saatgut.anker: Analogous to state breeding programmes such as India's Green Revolution from the 1960s.
daten.vorhaben.bio_saatgut.konkurrenz: The world's leading seed companies hold the patents, and trading partners control what may be imported.
daten.vorhaben.bio_medizintechnik.name: Medical technology cluster
daten.vorhaben.bio_medizintechnik.text: An industrial cluster for implants, diagnostics, imaging and medical robots, with universities, testing bodies and suppliers in one place.
daten.vorhaben.bio_medizintechnik.kehrse: Approvals are expensive and slow; the industry depends on a few components from abroad, and hospitals buy what the health insurers reimburse.
daten.vorhaben.bio_medizintechnik.anker: Analogous to the medical technology clusters of southern Germany and Switzerland, which grew over decades.
daten.vorhaben.bio_medizintechnik.konkur: Southern Germany, Switzerland and the USA have decades of head start; buyers trust established brands.
daten.vorhaben.bio_gentherapie.name: National gene therapy programme for rare diseases
daten.vorhaben.bio_gentherapie.text: Own gene therapies for rare hereditary diseases, developed, made and paid for at home: a cure where otherwise there is only lifelong treatment.
daten.vorhaben.bio_gentherapie.kehrseite: One treatment costs millions per patient: who gets it, and who pays? Ethics, waiting lists and a distribution conflict no government wins.
daten.vorhaben.bio_gentherapie.anker: Analogous to the world's most expensive gene therapies (prices of over two million US dollars per treatment).
daten.vorhaben.bio_gentherapie.konkurren: Pharmaceutical companies and research nations hold patents and data; experts migrate to where the labs are.
daten.vorhaben.chips_design.name: Chip design centre
daten.vorhaben.chips_design.text: A centre for chip design with universities and companies: the country designs, others manufacture. The first stage of any domestic semiconductor strategy.
daten.vorhaben.chips_design.kehrseite: Design without manufacturing depends on foundries in Taiwan and Korea, and the best people go to the big chip firms abroad.
daten.vorhaben.chips_design.anker: Analogous to the design centres of smaller chip nations such as Israel and Taiwan.
daten.vorhaben.chips_design.konkurrenz: Design data are coveted: industrial espionage hits chip firms first, and export controls decide who gets what.
daten.vorhaben.chips_euv.name: Own lithography machines (EUV)
daten.vorhaben.chips_euv.text: Machines that expose chips with extreme ultraviolet light: the most delicate technology in semiconductor manufacturing. Worldwide only a single company builds them so far.
daten.vorhaben.chips_euv.kehrseite: Thousands of suppliers around the world work on a single machine; without their licences and parts the country stands alone, and every export control hits the heart of the project.
daten.vorhaben.chips_euv.anker: Analogous to ASML in the Netherlands: the machines cost well over a hundred million euros each, backed by decades of development and a worldwide supplier network.
daten.vorhaben.chips_euv.konkurrenz: The Netherlands, the USA and Japan hold the key technology and control its export strictly; espionage around these machines is a matter of state.
daten.vorhaben.batt_zellfabrik.name: Battery cell factory
daten.vorhaben.batt_zellfabrik.text: A large-scale battery cell factory for electric cars, storage and industry: the step from assembly to making the most important component.
daten.vorhaben.batt_zellfabrik.kehrseite: Cells need lithium, cobalt and nickel from a few countries; fire risk and a price war with China hit every factory, and suppliers to combustion-engine makers lose their work.
daten.vorhaben.batt_zellfabrik.anker: Analogous to the battery cell factories in Europe, several of which suffered delays or insolvency after billion-euro promises (such as Northvolt in 2024/25).
daten.vorhaben.batt_zellfabrik.konkurren: Chinese manufacturers push down prices and hold the patents; espionage around cell chemistry is the order of the day.
daten.vorhaben.h2_elektrolyse.name: Green hydrogen: electrolysis park
daten.vorhaben.h2_elektrolyse.text: A park of solar, wind and electrolysers that supplies hydrogen for industry, fertiliser and transport: electricity that becomes storable and exportable.
daten.vorhaben.h2_elektrolyse.kehrseite: Hydrogen is expensive: it eats power and water, and buyers have yet to emerge; many projects of this kind exist only on paper.
daten.vorhaben.h2_elektrolyse.anker: Analogous to the hydrogen project in NEOM (Saudi Arabia, around 8.4 billion US dollars, start-up planned for the second half of the 2020s).
daten.vorhaben.h2_elektrolyse.konkurrenz: The Gulf states, Australia and Chile are building hydrogen parks on an even larger scale; Europe buys wherever it is cheaper.
daten.vorhaben.quanten_zentrum.name: Quantum technology centre
daten.vorhaben.quanten_zentrum.text: A research centre for quantum optics, quantum sensors and quantum communication, closely linked with universities and industry.
daten.vorhaben.quanten_zentrum.kehrseite: Basic research without market readiness: the best are poached by corporations and states, and the yield lies far beyond this term.
daten.vorhaben.quanten_zentrum.anker: Analogous to Germany's quantum programme (around three billion euros up to 2026).
daten.vorhaben.quanten_zentrum.konkurren: Quantum research is a race among the great powers; espionage and export controls decide who may take part.
daten.vorhaben.quanten_computer.name: National quantum computer
daten.vorhaben.quanten_computer.text: A quantum computer with thousands of error-corrected qubits for industry, encryption and research: no country runs anything like it continuously.
daten.vorhaben.quanten_computer.kehrseit: Quantum computers could break today's encryption: a race in which neighbours and allies listen in, and a computer whose usefulness no one can safely predict.
daten.vorhaben.quanten_computer.anker: Analogous to the quantum computer programmes of the big states and corporations; individual machines cost tens to hundreds of millions of US dollars.
daten.vorhaben.quanten_computer.konkurre: The USA, China and the big corporations lead; equipment and know-how are subject to export controls, and espionage targets every lab.
daten.vorhaben.robotik_offensive.name: Robotics and automation offensive
daten.vorhaben.robotik_offensive.text: Support for robots in factories, logistics and agriculture, plus training of technicians: whoever automates stays competitive against low-wage countries.
daten.vorhaben.robotik_offensive.kehrsei: Robots replace labour: industrial jobs are lost, the willingness to strike rises, and the profits go to business owners first.
daten.vorhaben.robotik_offensive.anker: Analogous to South Korea, the country with the highest robot density in the world.
daten.vorhaben.robotik_offensive.konkurr: The robotics leaders Japan, Germany and Korea sell their technology with maintenance contracts; China builds cheaper copies.
daten.vorhaben.nano_zentrum.name: Nanomaterials centre (graphene and composites)
daten.vorhaben.nano_zentrum.text: A centre for graphene, nanocoatings and composites with test stands and partners from aviation, construction and battery technology.
daten.vorhaben.nano_zentrum.kehrseite: Nanomaterials: the risks to health and the environment are still unexplored, the patents lie elsewhere, and many of the industry's promises have not come true.
daten.vorhaben.nano_zentrum.anker: Analogous to the EU's Graphene Flagship (one billion euros over ten years from 2013).
daten.vorhaben.nano_zentrum.konkurrenz: China, South Korea and the USA file the most patents; espionage in labs is common.
daten.vorhaben.reg_wohnungsbau.name: Housing programme
daten.vorhaben.reg_wohnungsbau.text: Affordable homes in the chosen provinces, built through the housing agency and private developers.
daten.vorhaben.reg_wohnungsbau.kehrseite: New building on the edge of town: journeys get longer, and builders push up prices when building capacity is scarce.
daten.vorhaben.reg_schulbau.name: School building programme
daten.vorhaben.reg_schulbau.text: New and extended schools in the chosen provinces, so that classes get smaller and journeys shorter.
daten.vorhaben.reg_schulbau.kehrseite: Buildings alone do not make a good school: teachers are missing, and running costs stay with the state.
daten.vorhaben.reg_krankenhaus.name: Hospital building programme
daten.vorhaben.reg_krankenhaus.text: New clinics and emergency departments in the chosen provinces, where the nearest doctor is far away today.
daten.vorhaben.reg_krankenhaus.kehrseite: A hospital without doctors is a building: staff and operation cost more than construction, and small hospitals never pay off.
daten.vorhaben.reg_wasser.name: Water mains, storage and treatment plants
daten.vorhaben.reg_wasser.text: Pipes, storage and treatment plants for the chosen provinces, where dry spells and network losses hit hardest.
daten.vorhaben.reg_wasser.kehrseite: Water that arrives here is missing elsewhere: the dispute grows downstream, and farmers pay for pipes that cities use.
daten.vorhaben.reg_damm.name: Dams and irrigation
daten.vorhaben.reg_damm.text: Dams, canals and irrigated fields in the chosen provinces: power, water and harvest from a single source.
daten.vorhaben.reg_damm.kehrseite: Villages and fields vanish in the reservoir, and less is left downstream: Iraq and Syria count every cubic metre.
daten.vorhaben.reg_strassen.name: Road and bridge building
daten.vorhaben.reg_strassen.text: Roads, bridges and bypasses in the chosen provinces: shorter journeys for people and goods.
daten.vorhaben.reg_strassen.kehrseite: More road attracts more traffic: land take, dust and guarantees to private operators bind the budget.
daten.vorhaben.reg_bahn.name: Rail expansion
daten.vorhaben.reg_bahn.text: New lines, electrification and stations in the chosen provinces.
daten.vorhaben.reg_bahn.kehrseite: Tracks take years and routes: farmers along the line lose land, and without trains and staff the line stays empty.
daten.vorhaben.reg_strom.name: Grid expansion
daten.vorhaben.reg_strom.text: Power lines and substations in the chosen provinces, so that power arrives and outages become rarer.
daten.vorhaben.reg_strom.kehrseite: Routes cross pastures and protected areas; residents sue against pylons.
daten.vorhaben.reg_breitband.name: Broadband and mobile
daten.vorhaben.reg_breitband.text: Fibre and radio masts in the chosen provinces, even where no one invests of their own accord.
daten.vorhaben.reg_breitband.kehrseite: For small places the roll-out never pays off: it remains permanently dependent on subsidies.
daten.vorhaben.reg_foerderung.name: Regional aid
daten.vorhaben.reg_foerderung.text: Commercial land, grants and incentives for businesses in the chosen, structurally weak provinces.
daten.vorhaben.reg_foerderung.kehrseite: Grants attract free-riders: some businesses come only for the money, and the charge of clientelism is close at hand.
daten.vorhaben.reg_wiederaufbau.name: Reconstruction and earthquake retrofitting
daten.vorhaben.reg_wiederaufbau.text: Rebuilding destroyed neighbourhoods and reinforcing vulnerable buildings in the chosen provinces, under the building inspection rules.
daten.vorhaben.reg_wiederaufbau.kehrseit: Promise against delivery: every delay is read as a broken promise, and building demand drives up prices.
daten.vorhaben.reg_stadterneuerung.name: Urban renewal: neighbourhoods and old towns
daten.vorhaben.reg_stadterneuerung.text: Streets, pipes and buildings in run-down neighbourhoods of the chosen provinces are renewed; residents get better homes, the neighbourhood a better reputation.
daten.vorhaben.reg_stadterneuerung.kehrs: A better neighbourhood becomes more expensive: rents rise, and those who already lived there are pushed out.
daten.vorhaben.reg_kultur.name: Restoration programme for sites
daten.vorhaben.reg_kultur.text: All catalogued sites in the chosen provinces are restored together: structure, roof and protection against damp and visitors.
daten.vorhaben.reg_kultur.kehrseite: Ties up restorers and building capacity; the sites are partly closed during the work, and tourism suffers.
daten.vorhaben.sperre.mil_f35.text: Blocked: the S-400s are in the country (NDAA §1245, CAATSA). They must be handed over first.

daten.vorhaben.zitat.wunder_antakya.text: … that the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch.
